title: hypervisor on macos: a VM/hypervisor won't start (nested virt / VT-x disabled)
scenario: On macos, a virtualization problem: a VM/hypervisor won't start (nested virt / VT-x disabled). Symptom: 'VT-x is not available / hypervisor error'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'nested_virt' for hypervisor on macos
expected_reasoning: A hypervisor that won't start usually lacks CPU virtualization (disabled in BIOS or nested-virt off).
Confirm the capability at the CPU/host level before touching the guest config.
Enable the correct layer (host nested virt / firmware) or pick a compatible accel.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'a VM/hypervisor won't start (nested virt / VT-x disabled)' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('nested_virt') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.

ground_truth.signal: VT-x is not available / hypervisor error

possible_mistakes: Force KVM accel on a host without vmx/svm.
Blame the guest image for a host capability gap.
hints: vmx (Intel)/svm (AMD) in cpuinfo prove hardware virt is available to the host.
Nested virt must be enabled on the parent hypervisor for a VM-in-VM.
reference_solution: Confirm CPU virt at host level
alternative_solution: Fall back to a software/emulated accel (slower) if hardware virt truly isn't available.
edge_cases: Hyper-V present steals VT-x from VirtualBox on Windows — they can't both use it.
goal: Virtualizzazione: a VM/hypervisor won't start (nested virt / VT-x disabled). Rendi avviabile la VM risolvendo la causa a livello host.
